title: Full protein sequence mapping using mass spectrometry
protocol: Treat protein sample with dithiothreitol (DTT) to break disulfide linkages between cysteine residues.
Heat sample at 51 degrees Celsius for 1.5 hours.
Let the sample cool to room temperature.
Add iodoacetamide in ammonium bicarbonate buffer and place in the dark at room temperature for 30-45 minutes.
Add a second aliquot of DTT to quench excess iodoacetamide.
Heat the sample at 51 degrees Celsius for 1 hour.
Let the sample cool to room temperature.
Use Endoproteinase Lys-C or trypsin to digest proteins into peptides.
Add enzyme at a ratio of 1:20 (enzyme:protein) and let incubate at room temperature for 6-9 hours.
Digest the protein with proteases for maximal amino acid sequence coverage.
Burn off the polyimide coating of about 2cm of the capillary using a small flame.
Use a laser puller to create a bottleneck in the clear glass section with a diameter of approximately 4um.
Make up a slurry of 5um C18 packing material in 80:20 acetonitrile:isopropanol.
Load the packing material behind the bottleneck using a pressurized stainless steel cylinder.
Pack approximately 6-7cm of packing material behind the bottleneck.
Use the laser puller to pull an electrospray tip approximately 2-3mm after the bottleneck such that the tip is approximately 5um in diameter.
Condition the column by loading 5pmol of angiotensin onto the column and running three short RP-HPLC gradients.
Load an aliquot of the proteolytic digest onto the microcapillary column using the pressurized stainless steel cylinder.
Cut a piece of 360x75um fused silica that is approximately 7-8cm in length.
Burn the polyimide coating off the very end of the capillary about 3-5mm using a small flame.
Pack licrosorb material into the clear end of the capillary and then burn with a micronox flame until licrosorb is melted but still porous.
Make a slurry of 5-20um C18 packing material in 80:20 acetonitrile:isopropanol.
Pack approximately 3-5cm of the packing material behind the frit using a pressurized stainless steel cylinder.
Condition the column as in step 6.
After loading the proteolytic digest onto the pre-column, wash with 0.1% acetic acid to remove any salts.
Connect the pre-column to the analytical column using a Teflon sleeve.
Connect the column apparatus to the HPLC solvent line.
Adjust HPLC pump flow to achieve a flow rate close to 57nL/min.
Apply high voltage (1.8-2kV) from the mass spectrometer to the stainless steel union on the HPLC waste line for electrospray mass spectrometry.
Run an RP-HPLC gradient of 0-80% organic solvent over a period of 40min-1.5hrs.
Set up MS/MS spectra acquisition in "data-dependent" mode using ion trap mass spectrometry.
Acquire one full range MS scan (300-2000 m/z) followed by the acquisition of ten data-dependent MS/MS scans during each experimental method.
Search MS/MS spectra against a database containing the full amino acid sequence of the target protein.
Include +80 amu variable modification for phospho modifications on S, T, and Y residues in search parameters.
Include +57 amu static modification for carbamidomethylation on cysteine residues in search parameters.
Manually validate all phosphopeptide hits to confirm phosphorylation site positions.
Eliminate false positive database hits below the top-scoring thresholds manually.
Pack an IMAC column using 360x100 or 360x150um fused silica depending on capacity needs.
Frit with licrosorb as described previously for packing the IMAC column.
Make a slurry of POROS MC 20 packing material in water.
Pack approximately 5-8cm of POROS MC 20 slurry behind the frit using a pressurized stainless steel cylinder.
Esterify the peptides to eliminate binding carboxylic acid side chains to the IMAC column.
Prepare a solution of 2M methanolic hydrochloride by adding 160uL acetyl chloride dropwise to 1mL anhydrous methanol while stirring under a ventilation hood.
Let the solution incubate, stirring, for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Dry down the peptide sample completely and add approximately 40uL of the 2M methanolic HCl to the sample tube.
Let sit at room temperature for 1-1.5 hours. Dry sample again.
Repeat treatment with fresh methanolic HCl. Let sit at room temperature for 1 hour.
Dry sample for last time and reconstitute in approximately 30uL of 1:1:1 acetonitrile: methanol: 0.01% acetic acid.
Prepare IMAC column by rinsing with ddH2O for 10 minutes at 20uL/min using a pressurized stainless steel cylinder.
Rinse column with 50mM EDTA for 5 minutes at 20uL/min.
Rinse again with ddH2O for 5 minutes at 20uL/min.
Activate column by rinsing with 100mM FeCl3 for 10 minutes at 20uL/min.
Load entire sample onto IMAC column slowly (approx 1uL/min).
Rinse column with 1:1:1 acetonitrile: methanol: 0.01% acetic acid (15min at 1uL/min).
Rinse column with 0.01% acetic acid for 15 minutes at 1uL/min.
Attach the RP-HPLC pre-column to the top of the IMAC column using a Teflon sleeve.
Elute the phosphopeptides off of IMAC column using 15uL of 100-200mM ascorbic acid at 1uL/min.
Detach pre-column and wash with 100% HPLC Solvent A for approximately 15 minutes.
Attach pre-column to analytical column using a Teflon sleeve.
Run LC-MS/MS analysis as described above.
